AssayWatch report

2026-10-27

Registry status: 178 active, 16 draft. `draft` is a maintainer sign-off, not a data check: 13 of the 16 drafts here already carry a verified DOI, a taxid and a design year with no open review question. What does vary between entries is oligo provenance, flagged in the note column of every row below.

Previous successful run: 2026-10-26 (1 day earlier).

Detected means predicted to amplify. The denominator is evaluable records only: both primers landed in the right orientation and size range. Records with no amplicon, or too many undetermined bases to judge, are excluded and counted separately. Intervals are Wilson 95%, pooled and per lineage alike. A pooled flag needs the upper bound of the recent interval to fall below the threshold. Declining means the share has also fallen from the baseline (that is drift); low coverage means below threshold without a measurable fall.

A lineage can also flag an assay whose pooled share clears the threshold — that is the point of measuring per lineage. Such a row is marked with its pooled status and its note names the lineage, its share and its own earlier share. The lineage rule is an exact binomial test against the threshold, Holm-adjusted within the assay, so it is looser than the pooled rule, and nothing controls error across assays: read an override as a reason to look at that clade rather than as a measurement of the assay.

Duplication check: 21 of 76 flagged assays still hold when duplicated records are discounted (each distinct binding-site footprint counted once, and the sample size cut to the number of footprints). The note on each assay that did not hold says which test it failed.

Detection against threshold

Every assay with an evaluable recent window, worst first. Left: where the recent detected share sits against the threshold. Right: how far it has moved from baseline. A flag rests on the two together, so the tables below are this figure read row by row.

This flag does not hold up: with only 34 independent observations (one per footprint) the interval around the 96% detected share is 83%-99%, which no longer rules out the 90% threshold. The failing records may well be real; what this says is that the SHARE failing may reflect how many near-identical records were deposited rather than how much of the population the assay misses.

Excluded: 1 indeterminate, 32399 no_amplicon

ASTROVIRUS_RdRp_Chu_2008 — Run as published, this nest detects 36.3% of the 2,901 records both rounds can be judged on: round 1 reaches 45.7% and round 2 80.1% on its own. Round 2's own figure is what it would do as a DIRECT PCR; within the nest 43.8% of that coverage is unreachable, because round 1 escapes on those records and leaves the inner reaction no enriched template. The rounds share reverse, so their failures are not independent - an escape there takes both.

ENTEROVIRUS_ssRNA_VP3_VP1 — These entries are labelled as rounds of one protocol, but their amplicons do not nest: on 3,794 records scored by both, the inner product lies inside the outer on 53. A nested reaction amplifies the outer product, so these two cannot be running that way - either the round labels are wrong or they are separate assays that share a name. No conditional coverage is reported for them, because conditioning round 2 on a round 1 that does not feed it would invent a number. Curation, not a calculation.

Coverage gaps

These assays cannot be validated against sequence data because the sequence data does not exist. For wildlife pathogens this is usually the finding. An assay with no taxid was never searched: that is a registry gap, not a data gap.

Detection penalty per position

For the flagged assays, how much detection falls when a record mismatches at each oligo position - the cost of the mismatch, not how often it happens. The shaded band is the 3'-terminal zone, where a mismatch blocks extension rather than shifting Tm; an amber base is already degenerate. Full numbers, and the accession groups behind them, are in site-drift.md.
